value.lineage: The Extended Kalman Filter (Schmidt/Smith, NASA Apollo era, 1960s) reduced to a few hundred lines with static allocation for Arduino/Teensy-class hardware; shipped with a GPS position/velocity example whose data and reference implementation come from Rachel Blakeley's 'Extended Kalman Filter for GPS' (MATLAB). SMALL MECHANISM: predict, then update with a linearised measurement model.

value.built_to: estimate a hidden state (position, clock bias) from nonlinear noisy measurements on a machine with kilobytes of RAM
value.pressure: hidden state, measurement noise, nonlinearity (ranges), tiny memory and CPU budgets
value.success_means: the estimate converges to the true trajectory and the covariance shrinks; no dynamic allocation

value.pressure: noisy observation, hidden state, bounded memory
value.failure_condition: filter divergence: linearisation error or a bad noise model drives the covariance to inconsistency and the estimate away

cut.note: the extended Kalman filter with every decision made for a small fixed-point-free microcontroller: state and measurement sizes are compile-time constants (EKF_N, EKF_M) so every matrix is a stack array; the caller supplies the nonlinear prediction and its Jacobian (fx, F) and the measurement prediction and its Jacobian (hx, H), so the filter itself is only the covariance algebra; the innovation covariance is inverted by a Cholesky decomposition that reports failure, so a non-positive-definite S aborts the update instead of corrupting the state

provenance.grade_basis: Techne FOSSIL_PACKET.json PROVENANCE_GRADE where issued, else the record's handoff string mapped (populated per R34; Harmonia may re-grade)

organs.human_name: ekf_predict (184-200): memcpy(x, fx); FP = F P; Ft = F^T; P = FP Ft + Q; the _mulmat / _transpose / _addmat helpers (10-70)
organs.mechanism: the caller evaluates the nonlinear transition f at the current state and its Jacobian F outside the filter and passes both in; the filter copies the predicted state and propagates the covariance with two matrix products and an addition of the process noise, all in fixed-size arrays sized by the compile-time constants
assumptions: the linearisation around the current estimate is the caller's responsibility; keeping the filter ignorant of the model makes it a library of one struct and two functions
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: an EKF that fits an Arduino: no heap, no dynamic sizes, no model code inside
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: no symmetrisation of P after the update; round-off can make P asymmetric over many steps in single precision (the _float_t switch exists to choose double)
organs.human_prior: Kalman 1960; the EKF of the Apollo era (Schmidt), the record's lineage

organs.human_name: ekf_update (215-300): G = P H^T (H P H^T + R)^{-1} via invert() -> _cholsl (116-160, returns nonzero on a non-positive pivot); x += G (z - hx); ekf_update_step3 (199-206): P = (I - G H) P
organs.mechanism: the innovation covariance S = H P H^T + R is inverted by Cholesky decomposition (choldc1) followed by forward and backward substitution; a non-positive diagonal during the decomposition returns an error and the update returns false, leaving x and P as predicted; otherwise the gain is P H^T S^-1, the state is corrected by the gain times the innovation z - hx (with hx supplied by the caller from its measurement model), and the covariance is reduced by the Joseph-less form (I - G H) P
assumptions: S is symmetric positive definite whenever the model and noises are sane; a Cholesky failure is a better signal of a bad measurement or model than a NaN in the state
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the standard EKF update with a cheap, explicit sanity gate
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: (I - G H) P is numerically less stable than the Joseph form; no innovation gating beyond the factorisation check
organs.human_prior: the standard EKF equations; Cholesky inversion from Numerical Recipes (the attic's origin per the comments)

pressures.source_evidence: tinyekf.h ekf_update and _cholsl; the examples' data
pressures.condition: an organism fuses sensors into a state estimate on a microcontroller; the dynamics and measurements are nonlinear; memory is static; occasional measurements are inconsistent (a corrupt GPS fix); the score is estimate error and the absence of divergence
pressures.resource_or_constraint: stack arrays sized at compile time; no heap
pressures.failure_condition: divergence after a bad measurement, or memory that grows with the problem
pressures.world_punishes: an update that inverts S without checking; dynamic allocation
pressures.world_rewards: fixed-size arrays and an abort on a failed factorisation
pressures.observable_consequence: position error on the GPS example's data with a corrupted fix injected, for the update with and without the Cholesky abort; peak stack use
pressures.vacuity_condition: a linear model with consistent measurements
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: a desktop EKF with the Joseph form and gating (which costs what the target lacks)
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given the true trajectory must show zero error; the update without the abort must diverge on the injected fix; with the abort it must skip the fix and continue: the world must show all three
